question: Is there an opportunity to change course in Syria because of that?
true_answer_verbatim: There is an opportunity. To the extent President-elect Trump has said anything at all about this issue - he said during the campaign that there was a real opportunity for the United States to support Russia and the Assad regime in their battle against ISIS. And I presume that the president-elect probably understands that there is no Russian-Assad regime battle against ISIS, that the tactics being used by Russia and Assad against civilian populations are in fact a wonderful recruiting tool, a gift that keeps on giving for ISIS.
true_answer_paraphrased: There is an opportunity. While President-elect Trump has not said much about this issue, he did say during the campaign that there was a real opportunity for the United States to support Russia and the Assad regime in their battle against ISIS. I presume the president-elect understands that Russia and the Assad regime are not actually fighting ISIS, and that the tactics Russia and Assad use against civilian populations serve as a highly effective recruiting tool for ISIS.

options.text: There is an opportunity. While President-elect Trump has not said much about this issue, he did say during the campaign that there was a real opportunity for the United States to support Russia and the Assad regime in their battle against ISIS. I presume the president-elect understands that Russia and the Assad regime are not actually fighting ISIS, and that the tactics Russia and Assad use against civilian populations serve as a highly effective recruiting tool for ISIS.

There are no military opportunities left on the ground. With the rebel forces about to collapse, the United Nations Security Council in New York is completely paralyzed. Our only real option is to redirect all funding from Congress to the International Red Cross, UNICEF, and the World Food Programme. We need to strengthen the borders of Lebanon and Turkey, expand facilities like the Zaatari camp near Amman, and help allies like Germany and Greece manage the Mediterranean migration crisis.
options.why: Answer 1 affirms that there is an opportunity to change course in Syria and implies a continued strategic focus on fighting ISIS, whereas Answer 2 argues that no military opportunities remain and all funding should be redirected entirely to humanitarian aid.

options.text: I see no opportunity for us to fix this, and the White House needs to accept that. We have already wasted billions of taxpayer dollars repeating the same mistakes the Bush administration made in Iraq and NATO made in Libya. The Department of Defense must withdraw our special operations forces from the Euphrates valley immediately. The security of the Middle East is a problem for Ankara, Tehran, and Riyadh to solve, not Capitol Hill or London.
options.why: Answer 1 asserts that there is an opportunity to change course in Syria, while Answer 2 explicitly states that there is no opportunity to fix the situation.

options.text: I believe we have a clear opportunity to change our strategy right now. The incoming Republican administration in Washington needs to abandon the failed strategies of President Obama and Secretary Kerry. We need to recognize that Vladimir Putin and the Syrian Arab Army are the only forces successfully clearing radical groups like Al-Nusra from eastern Aleppo. If the Pentagon and the CIA stop funding fragmented rebel groups across the Levant, we can finally defeat the extremists threatening Palmyra and Damascus.
options.why: While both agree there is an opportunity to change course, Answer 1 opposes aligning with Russia and Assad by arguing they do not actually fight extremists, whereas Answer 2 explicitly advocates supporting them as the only forces successfully defeating radical groups.

rejections.text: We have an important opportunity to reverse our failures, but it requires immediate escalation. The State Department must end the unproductive peace talks in Geneva. Instead, we should set up a strict no-fly zone near the Turkish border and heavily arm the Free Syrian Army and Kurdish YPG fighters advancing toward Raqqa. We cannot allow Moscow, Hezbollah, or the Iranian Revolutionary Guard to set the terms. We need to completely ground the Syrian Air Force to protect civilians in Idlib.
